summary:
The "Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars" project utilizes open space agency data to develop a solution that locates and analyzes regions on Earth with geological, topographical, or climatic conditions similar to those on the Moon and Mars.

What did you develop? A multi-dimensional data analysis and comparison tool that cross-references terrain, mineralogy, ice/water presence, and extreme environmental factors to pinpoint accurate terrestrial analog sites.
How does it address the challenge? Rather than relying on superficial visual similarities, it integrates comprehensive scientific datasets to evaluate deep physical processes and environmental equivalents.
Why is it important? Earth serves as a safe, cost-effective natural laboratory. Identifying true analog sites allows scientists and engineers to test rovers, habitats, and life-support technologies, significantly reducing risks for future long-term human space missions.
details:
• How it works: Collects and cross-references spatial data (terrain, minerals, ice/water, climate) from NASA/ESA using machine learning algorithms and GIS to rank terrestrial "analog sites."
  • Benefits & Impact: Provides a safe "natural laboratory" to test rovers and life-support technologies, minimizing risks and costs prior to actual space missions.
  • Technologies used: Python (NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, GDAL), QGIS, JavaScript (Leaflet/Mapbox), alongside satellite data from the LRO and MRO orbiters.
  • Creativity: Automates the screening process using deep multi-criteria analysis (subsurface structure, microclimate) rather than relying on superficial visual similarities like traditional methods.
  • Factors considered: Scientific accuracy, feasibility for safe field access, and future database scalability.
